page: Vultr vc2-24c-96gb is a general-purpose cloud server belonging to the Cloud Compute family. It features an x86_64 Intel Xeon processor running at 2.0 GHz, configured with 24 shared vCPUs mapped from 12 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The system is equipped with 96.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Storage is bundled as a local 1600 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU hardware is present on this instance.

Performance benchmarks indicate a solid mid-tier profile for multi-threaded operations. The server achieves average multi-core performance, with a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 32078.94 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 7313.0. However, single-core performance is relatively weak, as evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 838.0 and a text processing score of 588.0. Memory bandwidth is stable, reaching 114.95 GB/sec for large-block read operations and 55.93 GB/sec for write operations. The local NVMe SSD and CPU architecture support average database operation throughput, with Passmark database operations scoring 6984.96 and Redis SET operations processing at 31.68 million operations per second.

Because this instance utilizes shared CPU allocation, it offers a cost-effective resource density for multi-threaded workloads that do not require dedicated, sustained CPU performance. The primary tradeoff is the potential for CPU steal time and lower single-core performance under shared resource contention. It is suitable for multi-threaded applications, software compilation, static web serving at 15.77 GB/sec, and medium-scale database operations. It can also handle light LLM inference tasks, processing 33.17 tokens per second for prompt processing on a 7B model.
